main_issue: Whether and when Agent D can cook strong-smelling salted fish in the shared kitchen without the smell disturbing A's work, B's clothes and C's laundry

A-B.evidence: Both complained about smell (T1, T2); B later said the Tue/Thu after 7 and weekend plan was 'fine with me' (T18), matching A's acceptance (T15). They never addressed each other directly.

A-C.evidence: C's laundry is on Mon/Wed/Fri, so C accepted the schedule (T13, T19); A accepted the same plan (T15). C's 'that works for me' (T13) responds to A's call hours (T11).

A-D.evidence: A asked for no strong-smelling cooking (T1) and D said it's just what they eat (T4). D then offered Tue/Thu after 7 and weekends (T14) and A said 'Yeah, that works for me' (T15).

B-C.evidence: Both complained of smell (T2, T3); both ended up endorsing D's schedule (T18, T19). They did not address each other.

B-D.evidence: B said the smell gets into clothes (T2) and offered a door/window workaround (T6). D proposed a schedule (T14) and B said 'That's fine with me' (T18).

C-D.evidence: D offered to avoid cooking when laundry is out (T8) and proposed a schedule fitting C's laundry days (T14). C replied 'Yes, that works for me' (T19).
